info.title: Airspace API Documentation
info.description:
# Introduction Airspace's V2 API is a RESTful API. Our API accepts JSON-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs. With this API you can build integrations for Order Creation, Quote Generation, Label Generation, and Active Shipment Monitoring. ## Getting started with the Airspace API 1. Check with your Airspace Account Manager representative if you have an account at Airspace. 2. Reach out to integrations@airspace.com to get an API token. Once a token is generated for your account it will not expire. 3. We will configure your account’s access to use our test environment. Use authorization type as **bearer token** before starting to make any requests. 4. **[Optional]** We can also configure [webhooks](#section/Webhooks) to send status updates back to your system. 5. Once development is complete reach out to us for end to end testing. 6. After a few successful rounds of testing we will go live with your integration. ## Environments Environment | URL | Description ---|---|--- Production | https://api.airspace.com/api/public/v2 | For production use. Communicates with our production environment. Requires configuration. Test | https://apitest.airspace.com/api/public/v2 | For development and testing. Generally behaves the same as production. ## Example Request ``` curl -X POST "https://apitest.airspace.com/api/public/v2/orders" -H "accept: application/json" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer **YOUR_API_KEY_HERE**" -d @api-data.json ``` ## Response Codes Airspace uses conventional HTTP response codes to indicate the success or failure of an API request. In general: - Codes in the 2xx range indicate success. - Codes in the 4xx range indicate an error that failed given the information provided (e.g., a required parameter was omitted, a charge failed, etc.). - Codes in the 5xx range indicate an error with Airspace's servers (these are rare). # Authentication You will need an API key to access the Airspace API. Please contact integrations@airspace.com for your key. Note: Once you have a token it will never expire. # Webhooks Airspace can send webhooks programmatically to inform you about updates to your Order. A webhook is an HTTP request used to provide push notifications rather than making API calls to know the status of your Order. Webhooks can be triggered by an event, for example, a change in order status. When this change occurs, Airspace makes an HTTP request to your URL configured for the webhook. To receive Airspace webhooks, set up a dedicated endpoint on your server as a webhook listener that can receive POST requests, then provide this endpoint URL to Airspace. Contact integrations@airspace.com to create or change your subscriptions. ## Webhook Payload Structure Each webhook notification sent to your endpoint contains a complete payload with order details and event information. The payload structure varies dynamically based on the order state: - **Regular Status Updates**: Milestone events for normal order progression (picked up, in transit, delivered, etc.) - **Order Cancellations**: Problem events with cancellation details and error codes - **Order Delays**: Problem events with delay information and updated ETAs ## Example Webhook Payloads ### Regular Status Update ```json { "message": "Order status is now in_route_to_destination. Contact integrations@airspace.com to manage webhook subscriptions.", "events": [{ "milestone": {}, "occurred_at": "2026-01-22T15:30:45.123Z" }], "errors": null, "updated_order_keys": ["status"], "order": { "tracking_id": "ATXYZ123ABC", "tracking_url": "https://apitest.airspace.com/asap/tracking/ATXYZ123ABC", "order_number": 9000001, "status": "in_route_to_destination", "current_segment": "delivery_drive", "company_name": "Example Company", ... } } ``` ### Order Delay ```json { "message": "Order has encountered a delay.", "events": [{ "event_type": "delay", "problem": { "code": "2-001", "description": "Changed shipment parameters", "delivery_eta": "2026-01-23T16:00:00.000Z", "note": "" }, "occurred_at": "2026-01-22T14:25:30.941Z" }], "errors": null, "updated_order_keys": ["estimated_pickup_time"], "order": { ... } } ``` ### Order Cancellation ```json { "message": "Order has been canceled.", "events": [{ "problem": { "code": "2-007", "description": "Nothing to Pick Up or Shipment Not Ready/Uncontrollable delay at pickup", "delivery_eta": null, "note": "Shipment no longer needed" }, "occurred_at": "2026-01-22T16:45:10.525Z" }], "errors": null, "updated_order_keys": ["cancelled_at", "status"], "order": { ... } } ``` ## Webhook Configuration Requirements To receive webhook notifications, ensure your endpoint: 1. Accepts POST requests with JSON payload 2. Returns a 2xx status code on successful receipt 3. Can handle the dynamic nature of the payload based on order state 4. Uses the `order.tracking_id` or `order.order_number` fields to identify orders 5. Handles all three event types (milestone, cancellation, delay) To configure webhook status updates, we need the following: - The endpoints URL to which you want the updates sent. - Password to access the environment (test, production, or both). - Authentication method, one of: - Username-password - Bearer token - OAuth - Content type (eg: JSON). - Request Method(PUT or POST). ## Order Statuses The following are order statues that are available to receive updates for via webhooks: **Note:** NFO/ Next Flight Out - an order that is scheduled to be shipped using a flight. Status Code | Status Description ---|--- `will_call` | Creates a will call order which has not been routed and needs to be activated later for fulfillment.

Order has an expiration time, typically 72 hours after creation. The expiration time can be changed as needed. `pending` | Creates a Quote which needs to be submitted for fulfillment. `customer_completed` | Creates an order in our system for fulfillment. `ops_acknowledged` | Our Operations team has acknowledged/reviewed the order. `available_for_pickup` | A driver has been assigned to the order. `in_route_to_pickup` | The driver is en route to pickup the order. `arrived_at_pickup_location` | The driver has arrived at the pickup location. `in_route_to_destination` | The driver has picked up the order and is en route to the airport (only for NFO orders). `accepted_by_airline` | The order has been successfully delivered to the airport and accepted the by the airline (only for NFO orders). `verified_onboard` | The order has been on boarded onto the plane (only for NFO orders). `reached_destination_airport` | The order has reached the destination airport (only for NFO orders). `available_for_recovery` | A driver has been assigned and the order is available to be picked up from the destination airport (only for for NFO orders). `in_route_to_recovery` | The driver is en route to pick up the order from the destination airport (only for NFO orders). `arrived_at_recovery_location` | The driver has arrived to pick up the order from the destination airport (only for NFO orders). `recovered_from_airline` | The driver has picked up the order from the destination airport and is en route to deliver the order to the destination address (only for NFO orders). `arrived_at_destination` / `arrived_at_destination2` | The driver has arrived at the destination address.

**NOTE:** arrived_at_destination is for drive only orders, arrived_at_destination2 is only for NFO orders. `delivered` | The order has been delivered. `admin_canceled` | The order has been canceled.

upids.description:
UPIDs, or Unique Piece Identifiers, are mainly used to identify the pieces when there is no shipping label on them.
They can also be used for pieces with non-Airspace labels. A single piece can have multiple UPIDs.

Please check with your account management representative to know more.

custom_attributes.description:
Attributes are custom fields that will allow you to communicate specific requirements about your orders. They can be set up on Order level as well as on Address level. Additional charges may apply for some of the configured attributes, please clarify with your Account Manager.

Examples:
  - If you require ‘Airspace Protection Plan’ we can setup an order level custom attribute that will allow you to specify the dollar amount for the plan on the order.
  - If a TSA Certified Driver is required by any of the address locations, an address level custom attribute will allow you to specify this request on the address.

This feature is only available if your account is configured for it. Please contact your Account Manager for details.

service_type.description:
Requested delivery type.
- recommended - Route is selected based on your unique preferences and history.
- optimize_for_time - Route with fastest delivery time is prioritized over cost.
- optimize_for_cost - Most economical route prioritizes cost over delivery time.
- optimize_for_green - Route is selected based on environmental impact.
- drive_only - A drive only route which is adjusted for real time traffic and weather conditions.

airtrace_assignment_override.description: Override tracker assignment. If you try to assign an AirTrace Tacker to an order that already has it assigned, you may see an error. You may override this assignment if you have API access to this order. If the value is true, the AirTrace tracker will be removed from tracking its current assigned order. By continuing, you are acknowledging that you understand the risks. See [AirTrace](https://www.airspace.com/airtrace) for more information.

started_at.description:
The start time for the shipment’s viability. If timezone is not provided, the pickup address timezone
is assumed.

duration.description:
Viability duration of the shipment in hours. If not provided, the default value on the account
configuration will be used.

shipment_viability.description:
Viability window for a shipment. This is the time period for which the shipment is viable and we best
ensure for it to be delivered prior to its expiration. This feature is only available if your account is
configured for it. Please contact your Account Manager for details.

pickup_time.description:
Send a value in this key only if you want to specify a pickup time.
- For future orders, the value should be at least two hours in the future (in the timezone of the pickup location).
- For immediate pickup, leave blank.

patch.description:
If the order is in an updatable status (`will_call`, `pending`, `customer_completed`) updates are allowed in
specific scenarios.
- If order status is `will_call` or `pending` you can update any attribute that can be created.
- If a driver has been assigned to the order, it is up to our Operations team to manually approve your request.
- If a driver has not been assigned:
  - We allow updates to piece dimensions before pickup, as long as the assigned vehicle type is Car.
  - We don’t allow updates to orders if vehicle type is Van or Truck.
  - We allow updates to Point of Contact (for either address) and References up until driver solicitation.
- After an order has been submitted we don't allow:
  - Editing `has_dangerous_goods` flag
  - Adding or removing a piece

Contact operations if additional updates are needed.

Above conditions are subject to change without prior notice.

**NOTE:** Only provide attributes to update. If updating pieces or references you must include all items.
All previous pieces or references will be removed and replaced with new objects.

delete.description:
An order should be cancellable as long as it does not have an assigned driver, and it's in a cancellable
status (pending, customer_completed, ops_acknowledged, will_call). If the order cannot be canceled
automatically for any reason, we will notify our Ops team of your request for cancellation.

When an order is beyond ops_acknowledged, it cannot be canceled through the API. Contact Operations to
cancel the order in that scenario.
